newsitem.title: USA: Senior U.S. Republican says Gingrich should quit.
newsitem.headline: Senior U.S. Republican says Gingrich should quit.

text.p: A senior Republican in the U.S. House of Representatives said on Monday Newt Gingrich should step down from the post of speaker and Republicans should choose another leader.

The proposal was made on the eve of the House vote on speaker by Representative James Leach of Iowa, chairman of the House Banking Committee, who led an investigation of the Whitewater affair involving President Bill Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton. Leach's office said he would not vote for Gingrich.

Leach is the first member of the majority congressional Republican leadership hierarchy to say he would oppose Gingrich's re-election as speaker, and only the second House Republican of any rank to do so. The other is Rep. Michael Forbes of New York.
"He (Leach) will not vote for him (Gingrich) tomorrow. He is planning to vote for another Republican individual. He has not told me who that will be," said Leach spokeswoman Elise Downer.

In his lengthy statement on the issue, Leach said the speaker, third-ranking elected official in the U.S. government after the president and vice president, occupies too high an office to be clouded by controversy such as the House ethics breaches pending against Gingrich. He has admitted to violating rules governing the use of charitable donations for political purposes and to misinforming House investigators on that matter. A decision on punishment is pending before the House but would come well after Tuesday's speaker vote.

"The occupant of this position must be free of any shadow concerning allegiance to to the law or to the truth," Leach said. "Accordingly, for the country's sake I have concluded that the most responsible course of action for the speaker is to step down and for the members to choose another leader for the House."
